scenes.heading: Reading a brand deal contract before you sign it

sents.d: Reading a brand deal contract before you sign it
Exclusivity clauses and usage rights are where most bad creator deals hide.

An exclusivity clause (agreeing not to promote competing brands for a period) can quietly block other income for weeks or months — reading exactly how broad the competing-category definition is, and negotiating a shorter window if it seems excessive, protects future income you haven't even thought about yet.

scenes.heading: Paid ad usage is worth more

sents.d: Usage rights again matter here just as much as for other creative work: a brand wanting to run your content as paid ads indefinitely is worth substantially more than a single organic post, and should be priced and written into the contract accordingly.

Payment terms (net-30, net-60, on posting vs. on approval) vary a lot by brand size — larger brands often have slower payment cycles than they let on, so asking directly and getting it in writing avoids an unpleasant surprise.

take: Read exclusivity, usage and payment terms before you sign.
